title.narrative: TUI Academy Thailand phase 2

description.narrative: 160 disadvantaged youth age 17-24 (60% women, 40% men and diverse genders).

Financial: The project collaborates with partners in education and tourism to establish a robust network that champions youth economic empowerment. By partnering with government agencies specializing in vocational training, we lobby for updating existing curricula to address the specific needs of marginalized youth. We seek their commitment to integrate our proven interventions into their strategic work plans, ensuring long-term support for disadvantaged youth for gaining decent employment. In Phase 1, the life skills curriculum was integrated into partner educational institutions. In this phase, we aim to include green skills, sexual education, and employability skills. Building on successful government partnerships, we strengthen existing ties and engage new stakeholders to support job placement and address challenges such as seasonal employment. Youth will gain lifelong skills. These benefits extend beyond the project. Socially: We will develop an internal alumni database, so we can connect alumni with current participants to provide peer support mentorship. Led by volunteer alumni ambassadors, this network promotes sustainability and long-term impact.

From 2022-2025, Plan International implemented the TUI Academy Thailand Project (funded by RVO/FBK), in cooperation with TUI Care Foundation, ECPAT, and Robinson Club Khao Lak to support disadvantaged youth in tourism and hospitality in Phuket and Phang Nga. In Phase 1, 236 youth enrolled; 154 completed training and internships, and 109 secured decent jobs within six months. Life skills, English, and vocational training were provided, along with internships in roles such as F&B, housekeeping, and front office. Partnerships with 23 businesses and MoUs with four government agencies ensured high-quality training and sustainability. Key success factors included strong public-private collaboration, mentoring, and active community engagement, which boosted youth confidence and reduced dropout. Employers confirmed that graduates demonstrated greater workplace readiness and adaptability, aligning well with industry needs. This was echoed by the youth, trainers and family, who cited improved communication, self-confidence, and problem-solving skills.

Outcome 1: Increased Access to Dual Vocational Training for Young People • Stakeholder Engagement Meeting Stakeholders will be engaged through orientation sessions at the project's inception, to ensure understanding of the project’s goals and roles. Regular meetings will review progress and adjust implementation plans. Toward the project’s conclusion, sustainability discussions will facilitate a smooth transition to partners, ensuring the project's impact beyond completion. • Market scan A workshop will review labor market data and identify trends in the tourism and hospitality industry. This scan will guide the development of market-responsive training courses and help select appropriate training institutes. • Training Curriculum Adjustment Curricula will be reviewed and updated to align with industry demands, including green skills and gender equality. Life skills training will address specific challenges like sexual harassment and abuse, with resources from TUI e-academy and Plan International’s curricula. The adjusted curricula will be user-friendly for stakeholders. • Participant Recruitment The project will partner with local government agencies to promote the initiative and recruit youth. Participants will take aptitude tests and engage in discussions on gender equality. Success stories from previous participants will encourage engagement, particularly from parents and communities. • Pre-Employment Training Youth will receive comprehensive training in life skills, vocational skills, financial literacy, and gender equality. Courses will address market demands in the tourism sector, including green skills, and employability skills. Three months of training. • Provision of Internships Internships will be arranged with hospitality businesses, with participants receiving stipends and basic amenities. Businesses will be trained on gender equality, labor rights, and providing a supportive internship experience. Youth will report their progress through intern reports, and businesses will issue completion certificates. Three months of internship. • Graduation Ceremony and Career Connection The graduation ceremony will celebrate youth achievements and connect graduates with potential employers, serving as networking opportunity and showcasing the participants' skills to employers and increasing the chances of employment.
Outcome 2: Increased Support Services for Vulnerable Students and Their Families • Community Outreach Community engagement will focus on changing gender norms and promoting inclusion, particularly for young women and people with disabilities. Success stories from graduates will help build confidence and inspire participation • Provision and Facilitation of Comprehensive Welfare Support The project will offer allowances for transportation, accommodation, and meals, along with accident insurance for participants. It will also provide counseling services to address personal challenges and connect participants with appropriate support agencies. Case management will ensure participants receive continuous support, including childcare, shelter, and legal assistance, helping them transition into employment successfully. Outcome 3: Increased Employment of Young People in Tourism Destinations • Employer Engagement Strategy Employers will be engaged early to build partnerships and secure their commitment to providing employment opportunities.
• Training on Decent Work and Fundamental Labor Rights Employers will be trained on creating supportive and safe work environments, focusing on labor laws, gender equality, and the inclusion of marginalized groups. The training will ensure employers respect fundamental labor rights, creating a safe environment for youth. • Internship and Employment Counseling and Mentoring Youth will receive ongoing mentorship and counseling throughout their internships and employment. This will include strategic job matching and continued guidance to ensure career success and growth.
• Company Visits Regular visits to businesses offering internships or employment will gather feedback to improve support mechanisms and strengthen employer-youth relationships ensuring successful employment access and retention for youth.

SUMMARY In Thailand, youth unemployment and poverty rates are quite high, which lead to an increased risk of (sexual) exploitation. Disadvantaged girls and young women in particular are in a vulnerable position. At the same time, there is a high demand for motivated personnel in the growing tourism industry. To bridge this gap and empower young people, Plan International has established the TUI Academy in collaboration with the TUI Care Foundation. The program provides a holistic training package combining life skills, vocational training and an internship. Youth are educated on (risk of) sexual exploitation, financial support, and their rights. Plan engages businesses and communities to ensure decent work, protection, and inclusive employment in tourism. The project targets disadvantaged youth in Phuket and Phang Nga—particularly young women from ethnic minorities, school dropouts, teenage mothers, and those from low-income backgrounds—who are often excluded from education and employment.

Thailand faces a significant challenge with youth unemployment and approximately 1.4 million youth aged 15–24 (15%) are not in employment, education, or training (NEET). The NEET rate has steadily risen, from 14.4% in 2016 to 15.2% in 2021, with projections indicating a further increase. Girls are more vulnerable, being twice as likely to be NEET, due to social norms that assign women caregiving roles and early motherhood that hinders them to continue or return to education. Phuket and Phang Nga have a notably high proportion of NEET youth. These provinces continue to face issues such as school dropout rates and rising teenage pregnancies. These factors are key underlying causes of the high NEET rate of these provinces. Despite the high proportion of NEET youth and youth unemployment, both provinces face severe labor shortages, particularly in the hospitality and food service sectors, which account for 32.76% of employment in Phuket. In Q2 2023, despite 904 job vacancies for youth in Phuket, only 33 placements were made (3.7%). Phang Nga struggles with a lack of qualified workers in the hospitality and retail sectors. This labor market mismatch is driven by several factors, including education gaps, limited skills, and lack of awareness of job opportunities.

This project aims to enhance economic resilience among marginalized youth by equipping them with the confidence, knowledge, and skills necessary to secure meaningful employment in the tourism and hospitality industry, a sector contributing significantly to the gross provincial product in Phuket and Phang Nga and projected to grow further. The program will provide a holistic pre-employment training package, covering life skills, vocational expertise, employability techniques, and additional competencies like English and digital literacy. The project empowers youth with CSEC education, financial support, and internships, while engaging businesses and communities to ensure decent work, protection, and inclusive employment in tourism.
